title: the Glass Steppe Rising Anew
premise: Rosalind Halloran survives by siphoning memories from the wealthy and selling them back as secrets, but when the crown declares a hunt for memory-thieves, his gift becomes a death sentence. Hunted by the inquisitor Veyra Crane, Rosalind discovers the court beneath the Thornfell mountains has been buying souls — including the soul of the sister he thought dead, sold to pay his own debts. To reclaim her before the thirteenth moon, he must steal the one memory that anchors her to the underworld's throne. In the end, Rosalind trades his own identity for her freedom: she walks out whole while he becomes a stranger even to himself, alive but unremembered by everyone he saved.
about_author: Ada Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten letters in a mountain monastery before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive by trading away pieces of themselves.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. On a smuggler's road through Thornfell, Rosalind lifts a merchant's memory of a hidden vault and finds inside it a glimpse of his dead sister, alive and kneeling before an underground throne. Shaken, he takes the memory to his fence, Old Bram, who warns him the crown has posted hunters. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into dangerous hope.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Ash
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the city of Greyhollow, criers announce the hunt for the gifted; a neighbor is dragged away for remembering too much. Rosalind burns his caches of stolen memories to erase evidence, destroying years of leverage and identity in the process. Emotional beat: the first taste of survival's price — he must unmake himself to stay free.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Needle
chapters.summary: POV Veyra Crane. The crown's inquisitor interrogates a captured thief using a memory-extraction needle, learning of a 'Halloran' who deals in souls' worth of recollection. She recognizes the gift as kin to her own suppressed talent. Emotional beat: Veyra's cold efficiency cracks to reveal envy and fear of what she was made to forget.

chapters.title: Old Debts, Older Names
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind tracks the memory's origin to a debt-broker who confesses: thirteen years ago, someone sold a child's soul to the court beneath the mountain — signed with Rosalind's own name. He realizes his sister's sale paid for his survival. Emotional beat: guilt as revelation; the hunter learns he was the debt.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Twelve Remaining
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. An exiled undercourt priestess, Sefa, explains the bargain: the soul returns to its owner only if reclaimed before the thirteenth moon turns, after which it belongs to the throne forever. The price of entry is a memory freely given at each gate. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into obsession as the countdown begins.

chapters.title: What the Needle Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Veyra. Closing in on Rosalind, Veyra extracts a memory from his abandoned safehouse and experiences his childhood — including the sister, Wren, whom she realizes she once met. Doubt takes root about the hunt's true purpose: the crown feeds gifted souls to the undercourt. Emotional beat: loyalty to the crown beginning to rot.

chapters.title: The First Gate
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind descends through the Thornfell deeps, surrendering his happiest memory — a festival night with Wren — at the first gate. Below, he witnesses the court's economy of souls and nearly loses himself among the hollowed servants. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror; every step down costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: The Throne That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At the second gate Rosalind gives up his mother's face, and meets Wren — radiant, enthroned, and empty-eyed, anchored by the single memory the court keeps as her leash. She does not know him. He vows to steal that anchor memory from the throne itself. Emotional beat: heartbreak transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Theft of a Soul
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rosalind/Veyra. During the moon-turn ceremony, Rosalind infiltrates the throne vault while Veyra, having defected, holds off the hunt above. Rosalind steals Wren's anchor memory but the throne demands a replacement soul of equal weight. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice chosen in a heartbeat, no time for regret.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Freed, Wren climbs out of Thornfell carrying Rosalind's remaining memories as her only inheritance, guided by Veyra. She finds a man on the mountain road with kind eyes and no name, and begins telling him who he was — deciding which pieces to return. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; identity rebuilt as a gift rather than a possession.
